dimensions.note: 'KDI 경제전망, 2026 상반기' summary prose repeatedly ends a load-bearing forecast clause on a bare noun ('전망', '완화', '존재') rather than a finite predicate ('~할 전망이다', '~완화되었다'), e.g. a sentence built as '... 2.5% 정도 성장한 후 ... 성장을 나타낼 전망' with no closing 이다/verb. This truncated, headline-like sentence-final nominalization is a recognizable register marker of Korean institutional forecast writing — compresses the sentence while keeping the modal status ('전망'=forecast, not fact) legible from the noun itself. Worth carrying as a report-genre trait, not a general Korean trait: ordinary editorial or narrative prose would read as unfinished if it did this.
dimensions.evidence: "우리 경제는 2026년에 반도체수출 호조세와 내수 개선세로 2.5% 정도 성장한 후, 2027년에도 1.7% 수준의 성장을 나타낼 전망" — clause ends on the bare noun '전망', no copula.

dimensions.note: Causal-strength hedging is graded, not binary: a conditional risk clause stacks a conditional connective, a causal chain, and an explicit possibility marker in the same sentence rather than asserting the risk outright. This is the report-genre discipline the audience-facing econoi/BOK-storybook corpus enforces at a much simpler register (see ref:econoi-childrens-economic-newspaper, ref:bok-easy-economics-elementary) — here it is the same discipline surfacing in expert-register prose: state the mechanism, then explicitly flag that the outcome is a possibility, not a certainty.
dimensions.evidence: "중동 전쟁이 격화되거나 장기화되는 경우 원자재 수급 차질과 생산 비용 상승에 따라 성장세가 약화될 가능성도 존재" — conditional '경우' + causal '~에 따라' + explicit '가능성도 존재' (possibility exists), not a flat claim.

dimensions.note: Only the report's own summary/abstract prose was read, not the full body; sentence-to-paragraph rhythm across the full report (how long analytical sections run, where they compress vs. expand) was not observed and no claim is made about it here.

strengths: Sentence-final bare-noun compression on forecast clauses ('...전망', '...완화', '...존재' with no closing predicate) signals modal status (forecast vs. fact) through the noun itself while shortening the sentence — a report-register device, not general Korean style.

Risk/uncertainty clauses stack a conditional, a causal connective, and an explicit possibility marker rather than flattening a contingent outcome into a flat assertion — the same hedging discipline required across audience tiers, observed here at expert register.
weaknesses: Only the report's summary-level prose (as surfaced on the report's own web page) was read, not the full PDF body; paragraph-level rhythm and full-report information density are unverified and no claim is made about them.

This is one institution's forecast register; the bare-noun sentence-final compression trait is asserted as a report-genre pattern only after independent corroboration at a second institution (see ref:kiet-economy-industry-outlook, holdout) — it is not treated as established from this record alone.
